title: Two poems about the sea
text:
Poem A: Morning Sea

The sea wakes early, soft and slow,
and stretches in the sun;
it tickles toes along the shore
and giggles as they run.

It plays a game with fishing boats
and rocks them side to side;
it tucks small crabs in rocky pools
and gives the gulls a ride.

It sends a breeze to cool the town,
it splashes on the pier,
it sings a song of salt and spray
for anyone to hear.

At noon it dozes in the heat
and barely moves at all,
while children build a castle town
and chase a rubber ball.

It strings its shells like coloured beads
along the curving bay,
then waves goodbye with foamy hands
and slowly slides away.

But when the moon climbs up at night,
it hurries back to stay,
and hums the fishing town to sleep
until the break of day.

Poem B: Night Storm

Tonight the sea is a grey giant
pacing up and down the beach,
hurling its weight
against the harbour wall.
Boom.
Boom.
Boom.

The palm trees bend and whisper warnings.
Rain rattles on our tin roof
like a thousand marbles spilled.
Our cat has crept beneath the bed,
and even the clock ticks quietly,
as if it is listening too.

I press my face to the cold window
and count the boat lights in the bay:
one, two, three ...
but never four.

Father’s boat is the fourth light.

Mother hums an old song
to keep her hands from shaking.
I hold my breath
until my chest aches.

Then,
far out between the black waves,
a small gold spark
blinks,
and blinks again,
and grows.

Let the giant roar all night.
Father is coming home.
